country: # Wadden Sea spots lie in the national park: kite only in the marked zones

name: Sylt – Westerland
notes: Buhne 16 / Brandenburger Strand (lifeguarded beach): Germany's main wave spot, strong current between the groynes. Intermediate to expert riders. Also: K4 by Hörnum (flat channels at low tide, waves at high tide); Hörnum Möwennest on the Wadden side for E winds (around low tide).

name: Sylt – List (Königshafen)
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow flat water inside a national-park protection zone. Official rules (national park flyer 2021): set up, launch and land only on the kite beach, ride only inside the buoy chain, kite about 3 h either side of high tide.

name: Sankt Peter-Ording
notes: Ording beach (kite world cup venue): huge beach, flat to small waves, tide-dependent (about 2 h either side of high tide); strong current at times. Kite zones lie north and south of the marked bathing area in front of the main beach car park (pile rows and buoys), which is closed to kites; the middle of the sandbank is a bird area. Böhl, to the south, is the usual beginner side. Also: Büsum – Perlebucht further south (tidal lagoon, around high tide).

name: Cuxhaven – Kugelbake
notes: Elbe mouth: current and shipping lane. National park zone, about 3 h either side of high tide. Also: Sahlenburg west of town (large standing area, about 4 h either side of high tide).

name: Schillig
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow; ride around high tide. Kite school on site. Also: Hooksiel on the Jade further south (around high tide).

name: Norddeich
notes: Wadden Sea, kite area by the surf school; ride around high tide.

name: Norderney – Nordstrand
notes: Marked kite zone on the north beach; island rules limit the hours (not early morning). Also: Borkum and Langeoog north beaches (marked kite zones).

name: Flensburger Förde – Holnis
notes: Fjord beach, shallow for 80–100 m with sandbanks. Kiting is allowed left of the mole (facing the water); south of it is for swimmers only. Best in E–NE; SW–NW is the usual wind. Crowded with tourists in summer. Very low water after a strong E wind followed by W.

name: Laboe
notes: Kiel Fjord mouth; one of the few Kiel spots that works in SW. First 200–400 m is standing depth, mussel beds and ship waves over a sandbank at the channel edge. Kite only between the stone breakwater and the nature reserve to the east, outside the white swimming buoys. In the bathing season the beach in front of the harbour is closed to launching and landing (municipality, reported by Surf magazine; no official text found).

name: Heiligenhafen
notes: Experienced riders only. Best in W–NW (side-onshore, small steep waves over the bar), flat in E; S–SW is offshore. Sources conflict on where: a shop guide says kiting is only allowed at the Graswarder beach east of the pier, behind the marina, and banned at Steinwarder and on the Binnensee; another guide shows a marked kite zone at east Steinwarder. No official text found: ride only where kite signs are posted, never in the swimmer zone. Wooden groynes, old jetty posts, nature reserve rules.

name: Fehmarn – Gold
notes: The beginner spot of the Baltic: huge standing-depth area, best in W–SW, nearly as good in E. Busy with schools; stones in the north part.

name: Fehmarn – Wulfener Hals
notes: Bay side: flat water, standing depth across the whole bay, best in E, gusty in W (buildings on the shore). Open sea side: choppy, not for beginners. A camping site runs the bay: one guide reports kiting only 18:00 to 10:00, daytime for courses only (no official text, check on site). Stones on the beach.

name: Fehmarn – Grüner Brink
notes: North coast: works from E through N to W, not in S. The nature reserve next to it is closed to kiters; outside the marked summer swimming areas only. Shared with a dog beach.

name: Pelzerhaken
notes: Designated kite zone on a guarded sandy beach, standing depth, flat to small waves. Prevailing wind SW–NW; busy in summer.

name: Salzhaff – Pepelow
notes: Salzhaff: shallow flat-water lagoon, huge standing area, ideal for learning. Kite school on the Pepelow campsite; works in SW–N winds; free access; season mid-April to October.

name: Warnemünde
notes: Kite access at beach access 13, west of the pier (ostsee.de lists beach blocks 12–13 for wind and kite sports); rough waves in strong N–NW wind. Summer: swim zone marked by buoys and a crowded beach in July–August, so little room to launch. For advanced riders.

name: Wustrow
notes: Baltic side: waves (German Kitesurf Open venue). Bodden side: flat shallow water. Also: Saal on the Saaler Bodden (flat shallow water, kite school).

name: Zingst
notes: Sportstrand at the edge of town; choppy, deep enough for foiling.

name: Rügen – Suhrendorf (Ummanz)
notes: Bodden: shallow flat water, beginner-friendly.

name: Rügen – Dranske
notes: Wieker Bodden side: flat water. Also: Wiek on the Wieker Bodden.

name: Usedom – Karlshagen
notes: Sportstrand with kite school; waves in E winds, W winds are offshore. Keep clear of the swimming zone. Also: Peenemünde just north; Ückeritz on the Achterwasser for W–S winds.

name: Steinhuder Meer
notes: Mardorf / Weißer Berg on the north shore: about 500 m of standing area. Kiting roughly 20 Mar–15 Nov in the marked zone.

name: Dümmer
notes: Shallow lake; launch at the surf entry point (Rohrdommel).

name: Chiemsee – Übersee (Feldwies)
notes: Kite zone at Feldwies on the south shore (Tiroler Achen delta): works in W–N winds. Kiting only in the marked zone. Also: Chieming on the east shore (KBC kite club zone, W–NW winds).

name: Sylt – K4 (Hörnum)
notes: West beach at crossing 74 (big car park), 4 km north of Hörnum: named an official surf and kite beach by the national park. Flat channels at low tide, waves at high tide; strong coastal current. Ask a local school which tide suits you.

name: Sylt – Hörnum Möwennest
notes: Wadden side behind the Möwennest hostel: flat shallow water for E winds. National park rules (flyer 2021): kite only about 3 h either side of low tide and keep 300 m (kites included) from the Hörnum Nehrung bird area.

name: Dagebüll
notes: Wadden Sea, by the ferry pier; around high tide only.

name: Nordstrand – Holmer Siel
notes: Wadden Sea: about 5 h around high tide; groyne fields (Lahnungen) at low water.

name: Husum – Dockkoog
notes: Wadden Sea, around high tide. Busy in summer; no-go channel south of the point.

name: Büsum – Perlebucht
notes: Northern part of the Perlebucht only. The lagoon itself is cut off from the sea (flat in any wind) and advanced riders only (VDWS 5 / IKO 3); the shallows in front of it follow the tide, so ride around high tide. Sign in at the kite school; not for E winds (Büsumer Deichhausen then).

name: Cuxhaven – Sahlenburg
notes: Large standing area; about 4 h either side of high tide.

name: Otterndorf
notes: Elbe estuary: strong tidal current and shipping lane nearby; ride around high tide.

name: Dorum-Neufeld
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow: about 3 h either side of high tide. Channels are shipping lanes.

name: Wremen
notes: Wadden Sea, large standing area: about 3.5 h either side of high tide.

name: Butjadingen – Tossens
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow; about 3 h either side of high tide.

name: Hooksiel
notes: Jade, shallow; ride around high tide.

name: Neuharlingersiel
notes: Wadden Sea; about 3.5 h either side of high tide.

name: Dornumersiel
notes: Wadden Sea, shallow; marked 80 ha kite zone in the national park, kiting 3 h either side of high tide, open 1 May–15 Sep per the Lower Saxony tourism page (Unplug says from 1 June: the earlier date is kept as the official one). Kite school Vertigo on the beach. Intermediate level.

name: Borkum – Nordstrand
notes: Marked kite zone on the north beach; island rules limit the hours (not early morning).

name: Langeoog – Nordstrand
notes: Sportstrand on the north beach: waves at high tide, shallow at low tide; island rules limit the hours.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — second Flensburg Fjord spot

name: Flensburger Förde – Schausende
notes: Fjord spot next to Holnis (about 1 km): shallow standing area, boat traffic and occasional nets. Best in NE–E, less pretty than Holnis.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 3 km from Laboe

name: Stein
notes: Small beach on the east side of the outer Kiel Fjord: shallow flat water, standing area of about 200 m, little chop. Best in W–NW, gusty in E. Launch from the cliff side west of the loungers in summer. A surf school on the beach teaches kite.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — next to Heiligenhafen and Fehmarn

name: Großenbrode
notes: West beach: flat, standing depth in SW to N, stones west of the entry point (wear booties). South beach: NE to SE, small waves, standing area.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 3 km from Gold

name: Fehmarn – Lemkenhafen (Orther Reede)
notes: Flat, glassy shallow water in the Orther Reede for W–SW and S winds; kite school on site, wide dike for rigging.

name: Saal (Saaler Bodden)
notes: Shallow flat water almost everywhere; kite school (Kitesportschule Simon, water sports centre) on site; free access; SW and NW are the best side-shore winds.

name: Rügen – Wiek
notes: Wieker Bodden: flat shallow water.

name: Gahlkow
notes: Greifswalder Bodden: narrow beach, choppy and gusty; shallow up to about 800 m out; works from W through N to E. WSW wind is gusty: riders move 1 km west to Loissin (kitesafe school there). No school at Gahlkow itself.

country: # pro: cluster duplicate — 5 km from Karlshagen

name: Usedom – Peenemünde
notes: Choppy, deepens quickly; few facilities.

name: Usedom – Ückeritz (Achterwasser)
notes: Achterwasser by the harbour: standing area, choppy; best W–S.

name: Brombachsee
notes: Großer Brombachsee: occasional afternoon thermals. Kiting April–June and September–November.

name: Chiemsee – Chieming
notes: East shore, KBC kite club area: works in W–NW winds. Kiting only in the marked zone.

country: # pro: 8 km from Zingst (kept) — Darß coast
region: kite school in Prerow (visit-mv.com Kiteschule Darss + Surfspot Prerow); Nordstrand inside the national park
name: check zoning
Prerow
notes: Baltic side of the Darß: moderate waves, good with E winds. Kite school in town; the park beach to the north has protected zones, ask locally.

name: Strande
notes: Town beach on the west shore of the outer Kiel Fjord, easy from Kiel. One of the few Kiel spots that also works in S wind (guides). Ship traffic on the fjord: keep clear of the channel. Surf club beside it teaches windsurf; no kite school confirmed.

name: Heidkate
notes: Probstei coast: a surf school (VDWS centre) teaches kite on the beach; a guide calls it the hotspot of the area, with a sandbank about 200 m offshore. Wetsuit nearly all year. Not tide-dependent in practice (Baltic).

name: Hohwacht
notes: Bay of Hohwacht, beach by the harbour: chop and small waves, intermediate and up (guides); wind best from N to NE. Breakwaters in the water at the north end. No kite school confirmed on site.

name: Fehmarn – Orth (Orther Bucht)
notes: East shore of the Orther Bucht: big flat shallow areas either side of Orth village, a training arena for W winds (guides). Parking only at the small beach by the campsite. Same bay as Lemkenhafen but about 1.5 km away on the other shore: pick by wind and parking.

name: Fehmarn – Bojendorf (Wallnau)
notes: West coast: smaller, more forgiving waves than Westermarkelsdorf, a beginner-friendly spot in W to SW (kite guide); strong N wind is harder. Wallnau, reached through Bojendorf, is listed for N and SW wind, intermediate and up. The beach at Wallnau is a naturist beach: be discreet.

name: Fehmarn – Miramar (Fehmarnsund)
notes: On the Fehmarnsund strait by the Miramar campsite: W and E winds are accelerated along the strait. Tricky access between groynes and slipways. Wulfener Hals is the better choice when wind is enough (guides).

name: Fehmarn – Meeschendorf
notes: South coast east of Miramar: one of the few Fehmarn spots with side-onshore wind in E; waves stay moderate even above 25 kn (guide). Groynes on the Südstrand side.
